title: Responses event-model taxon & fuzz harness + staged mitigation blueprint
creator: Marina Lopez
description: Audit and engineering plan to catalogue behavioral divergences between OpenAI Responses event model and Redwood's Responses abstraction. Deliverables: (1) a taxonomy (taxon) of observable divergence classes, (2) a fuzz-test harness that exercises event-order, streaming fragments, toolcall boundaries, and structured-output edge cases, (3) mitigation scaffolding containing translation heuristics, signal tagging, and graceful degradation strategies, and (4) a canary rollout & telemetry plan to measure compatibility score during migrations.
acceptance_criteria: Taxonomy document completed with at least 8 divergence classes and representative examples
Fuzz harness runs deterministically in CI and identifies known regressions from previous audits
Mitigation scaffold implemented as a pluggable translation layer with feature flags
Canary plan defined with telemetry events and a compatibility scoring metric, runbook for automated rollback
PR to runtime with tests and a smoke canary in staging merged
progress_notes: 2025-11-04: Spike completed—mapped 3 high-frequency divergence patterns (stream chunk boundary toolcalls, truncated structured JSON, function-call metadata loss).
2025-11-07: Fuzz harness prototype (golang) can inject out-of-order events and simulate partial stream reconnections; needs deterministic seed control and corpus storage.
2025-11-09: Design review with PM/Docs—agreed to surface compatibility score as 'compatibility.delta' telemetry tag and expose to Console as a degradation alert.

2025-11-12: Implementation PR opened for translation-layer (runtime feature flag: responses.compat-bridge). Initial heuristics: event-reassembly, toolcall-sentinel headers, structured-output lenient parser.
2025-11-15: Security review requested for headers that carry toolcall routing hints (pending), flagged potential PII leakage in reassembly buffer—mitigation: buffer truncation + policy filter.
2025-11-18: Internal review notes: QA reported 2 flaky cases when simulating reconnect; recommended adding per-session sequence number and idempotency checks before canary rollout.
